author: DTrim99
body:
You're right that Arkansas's employer-pension exemption has no minimum age — PolicyEngine applies none (the 59½ test only gates traditional-IRA distributions, per Line 13 of the AR1000F instructions).

But the difference here is *character*, not age. Your AR1000F reports the $33,780 on **Line 16, "Non-qualified IRA distributions and taxable annuities"**, which is fully taxable — not Line 18 (employer pension plan / qualified IRA), which is what carries the $6,000 exemption. The instructions for Line 16 say to "report taxable lump-sum distributions, annuities, and traditional IRA distributions [including] early withdrawal of traditional IRA distributions on this line." Since the recipient is 52, a premature IRA distribution correctly lands on Line 16 and gets no exemption — consistent with your return.

PolicyEngine, by contrast, treats the TAXSIM `pensions` input as an employer pension (Line 18) and grants the $6,000 exemption. The `pensions` field carries no 1099-R distribution code, so there's nothing to tell an exemption-eligible employer pension from a taxable annuity or a premature IRA distribution — PE defaults to the former. (Separately, for a married-joint record the emulator splits the combined pension 50/50 between spouses, so it grants two $6,000 exemptions rather than the single $6,000 a one-recipient pension would get.)

So PolicyEngine is right for a genuine employer pension, but not for the non-qualified annuity/IRA that your return reflects. It's the same underlying convention question as #1145 — whether TAXSIM `pensions` should be treated as exemption-eligible on the state side.
